GA|Locust Grove.note: Henry County adopts the Georgia state codes by reference, so the mandatory state minimum governs. The City of Locust Grove's own page still lists 2018 editions (Jan 1, 2020) — that page is out of date; the law in force is the state code.
GA|Locust Grove.source: Henry County Unified Land Development Code §1.07.06 (adopts the state codes, incl. future editions, by reference)

SC|Spartanburg.note: Follows the South Carolina statewide code — mandatory in Spartanburg County; the county cannot adopt a different edition.
SC|Spartanburg.source: SC Building Codes Council — 2024 Code Adoption Notice (Aug 26, 2025)

AK.name: Alaska Building Code (13 AAC 50.020)
AK.note: Adopted by the State Fire Marshal for commercial, industrial, institutional, public and 4+ unit residential buildings.
AK.source: AK Dept. of Public Safety, Div. of Fire and Life Safety — 13 AAC 50.020

AL.note: The state code covers only state property, schools, hotels/motels and theaters; all other buildings follow the city/county code.
AL.source: Alabama Dept. of Finance, Division of Construction Management — State Building Code

AR.name: Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, Vol. II
AR.source: AR State Fire Marshal — 2021 Arkansas Fire Prevention Code Rules

AZ.note: Arizona has no statewide building code; each city/county adopts its own edition.

CA.name: 2025 California Building Code (Title 24, Part 2)
CA.note: California's own code, built on the 2024 IBC with California amendments.
CA.source: CA Building Standards Commission — code history + Information Bulletin 26-01

CO.note: Colorado has no statewide building code; adoption is by city/county.
CO.source: Colorado Office of the State Architect — Building Codes

CT.name: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code
CT.source: CT Dept. of Administrative Services, Office of the State Building Inspector

DC.name: 2017 DC Construction Codes
DC.source: DC Department of Buildings — DC Construction Codes

DE.note: Building-code authority sits with Delaware's three counties and municipalities.

FL.name: Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023)
FL.note: The 9th Edition's adopting rule was still in rulemaking when this was verified — its date is scheduled, not final.
FL.source: Florida Building Commission — 2026 FBC Workplan; Rule 61G20-1.001

GA.name: Georgia State Minimum Standard Building Code
GA.note: The Georgia state minimum is mandatory in every Georgia county. A further Georgia Amendments package takes effect Jan 1, 2027 — it is not an edition change.
GA.source: Georgia Department of Community Affairs — Current State Minimum Codes; 2024 IBC Amendment Packet (eff. Jan 1, 2026)

HI.name: Hawaii State Building Code
HI.note: Counties adopt the state code with local amendments under HRS §107-28.
HI.source: HI State Building Code Council (DAGS) — Building Code Rules

IA.name: Iowa State Building Code
IA.note: Applies per Iowa Code ch. 103A (state-owned/funded and covered jurisdictions); some localities adopt their own code.
IA.source: IA Dept. of Inspections, Appeals & Licensing — ARC 9474C

ID.name: Idaho Building Code
ID.source: Idaho Building Code Board / DOPL — IDAPA 24.39.30; Idaho Code §39-4109

IL.note: No single statewide edition. Since Jan 1, 2025 state law sets an IBC-stringency floor for local codes, and a state default covers commercial buildings where no local code exists — the edition enforced on a given job is the local one.
IL.source: Illinois Capital Development Board — Building Codes and Regulations

IN.name: 2014 Indiana Building Code
IN.note: Built on the 2012 IBC — the oldest base edition in force in any state.
IN.source: IN DHS, Fire Prevention & Building Safety Commission — 675 IAC 13-2.6

KS.note: Kansas is a home-rule state; adoption and enforcement are local.
KS.source: Kansas Dept. of Administration, OFPM; KS Corporation Commission

KY.name: Kentucky Building Code
KY.source: KY Dept. of Housing, Buildings & Construction — 815 KAR 7:120

LA.name: Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code
LA.note: The 2024 adoption was approved as rule language and published as a Notice of Intent (Aug 20, 2026 Louisiana Register); final promulgation had not been located when this was verified — its date is scheduled, not final.
LA.source: LA State Uniform Construction Code Council — LAC Title 17 §§101/103

MA.name: 780 CMR — Massachusetts Building Code, Tenth Edition
MA.source: MA Board of Building Regulations & Standards — Tenth Edition 780 CMR

MD.name: Maryland Building Performance Standards
MD.source: MD Dept. of Labor, Building Codes Administration — COMAR 09.12.51

ME.name: Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code
ME.source: ME Technical Building Codes & Standards Board / State Fire Marshal — MUBEC

MI.name: Michigan Building Code
MI.source: MI LARA, Bureau of Construction Codes — Part 4 Rules (2022-57 LR)

MN.name: 2020 Minnesota Building Code
MN.source: MN Dept. of Labor and Industry — Minnesota Rules ch. 1305

MO.note: Missouri has no statewide building code at all; adoption is purely local and many rural counties have no code. The state publishes a county-by-county dataset precisely because there is no single answer.
MO.source: Missouri Legislature — RSMo §67.280 (local adoption authority); State of Missouri Data Portal, county building-code dataset

MS.note: Localities adopt one of the last three MBCC-adopted editions or opt out; the State Fire Marshal's own adoption covers only state-owned, public-assembly and high-rise buildings. No statewide edition can be stated.
MS.source: Mississippi Insurance Dept. / State Fire Marshal; Miss. Code §17-2-4

MT.name: Montana Building Code
MT.source: MT Dept. of Labor & Industry, Building Codes Program — Current Codes (ARM Title 24 Ch. 301)

NC.name: 2018 North Carolina Building Code
NC.note: The 2024 NC Building Code (2021 IBC base) is formally adopted, but by Session Law 2025-2 it takes effect 12 months after State Fire Marshal certification, which has not occurred. No effective date exists yet — any date in circulation is unconfirmed.
NC.source: NC Office of the State Fire Marshal — Codes: Current and Past

ND.name: North Dakota State Building Code
ND.source: ND Dept. of Commerce, Div. of Community Services — Building Codes

NH.name: New Hampshire State Building Code
NH.note: Applicants may elect the prior (2021) code through Dec 31, 2026.
NH.source: NH Building Code Review Board — RSA 155-A (HB1159, 2026)

NJ.name: NJ Uniform Construction Code — Building Subcode
NJ.note: A prior-code grace period runs to Feb 17, 2027.
NJ.source: NJ Dept. of Community Affairs, Div. of Codes & Standards — Current Construction Codes

NM.name: 2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code
NM.source: NM Regulation & Licensing Dept., Construction Industries Division — 14.7.2 NMAC

NV.note: Nevada has no general statewide IBC; adoption is local. State pieces (fire marshal references, state buildings) use their own editions.

NY.name: 2025 Building Code of New York State
NY.note: New York City has its own separate construction codes.
NY.source: NY Dept. of State / State Fire Prevention & Building Code Council — 2025 Uniform Code

OH.name: 2024 Ohio Building Code
OH.note: Ohio's own code: the 2024 Ohio Building Code is built on the 2021 IBC with Ohio amendments — the edition in force is the 2021 IBC, not a 2024 IBC.
OH.source: Ohio Board of Building Standards — 2024 Ohio Building Code Rules

OK.name: Oklahoma Uniform Building Code
OK.source: OK Uniform Building Code Commission — IBC Adoptions; OAC 748:20-2-1

OR.name: 2025 Oregon Structural Specialty Code
OR.note: Oregon's own code, built on the 2024 IBC. The 2022 code could be used during phase-in until Apr 1, 2026.
OR.source: Oregon Building Codes Division — Commercial Structures / adopted codes

PA.name: Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code
PA.source: PA Dept. of Labor & Industry — UCC; Review & Advisory Council 2021 ICC Adoption Final Report

SC.name: 2021 South Carolina Building Code
SC.note: South Carolina codes are mandatory in every county and municipality; local jurisdictions cannot adopt a different edition, and only Council-approved modifications are valid.
SC.source: SC Building Codes Council (LLR) — Building Codes in Effect

SD.name: South Dakota building code standard (SDCL 11-10)
SD.note: A statutory standard, not a state-administered code: local ordinances for non-residential buildings must comply with the 2024 IBC (local amendments allowed); buildings in jurisdictions without an ordinance must be designed to it.

TN.name: Tennessee statewide minimum building code
TN.note: Tennessee sets a statewide minimum (2021 IBC, eff. Apr 17, 2025), but local governments with their own enforcement programs adopt and enforce their own editions — the edition on a given job is the local one in much of the state. No single edition can be stated for every Tennessee job.
TN.source: TN Dept. of Commerce & Insurance — Rule Ch. 0780-02-02 (filed Jan 17, 2025)

TX.name: Texas municipal commercial code (Loc. Gov't Code §214.216)
TX.note: Section 214.216 makes the 2012 IBC the municipal commercial code floor, but Texas cities adopt and enforce their own editions and most large cities are on much newer codes. The edition on a given job is the city's — no single edition can be stated.
TX.source: Texas Legislature — Loc. Gov't Code §214.216; TDLR Industrialized Housing & Buildings

VA.name: Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code
VA.source: VA Dept. of Housing & Community Development — Codes

VT.name: 2025 Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code
VT.note: Applies to public buildings (20 V.S.A. Ch. 173).
VT.source: VT Dept. of Public Safety, Div. of Fire Safety

WA.name: Washington State Building Code
WA.note: The May 3, 2027 date is the SBCC's announced schedule (CR-102 filed May 6, 2026); the final adoption filing for the IBC chapter had not been separately confirmed when this was verified — the date is scheduled, not final.
WA.source: WA State Building Code Council — State Codes (ch. 51-50 WAC)

WI.name: Wisconsin Commercial Building Code
WI.source: WI Dept. of Safety & Professional Services — SPS 361-366; Fall 2025 Newsletter

WV.name: West Virginia State Building Code
WV.note: The state sets the edition; enforcement is by adopting local jurisdictions.
WV.source: WV State Fire Commission — Title 87 Series 4 (87CSR4)

WY.note: Wyoming has no single statewide building code; adoption and enforcement are local.
WY.source: WY Dept. of Fire Prevention & Electrical Safety — Rules Ch. 1
